Habermas's "law as medium" is formally rational steering law that coordinates the economic and administrative subsystems through money and power, integrating action instrumentally rather than through shared norms. "Law as institution" is lifeworld-rooted normative law (e.g., constitutional rights, family law) that depends on communicative justification and preserves solidarity and mutual understanding. The distinction thus contrasts system-integrating steering law with lifeworld-protecting normative law.
